intro: An Irish maker of steel-framed pods, built and fitted out in its factory in Co. Meath and craned into place: garden studios, garden homes, family homes and extensions.
standfirst: Every pod starts from a base model and is then designed with you, from the layout to the level of insulation. These are The Pod Factory's own photographs of finished pods.

costs.title: How The Pod Factory prices a pod.
items: No price list is published. Every pod is bespoke, so the supplier prices each one for the client; ask for a quote.
Pods are delivered by lorry and craned into place, anywhere with access for the trucks and crane.
The site's groundworks must be completed before the pod arrives. The site does not say whether these are in the quote; ask.
Water and electricity are connected to the services already on site, as part of the installation.
ATC radiators are fitted as standard. Solar panels, heat pumps and triple glazing can be added.
costs.note: Lead time: the supplier's pages give about 10 weeks to delivery (modular homes page) and as little as twelve weeks (FAQ) once the design is finalised. Its showroom near Dunshaughlin, Co. Meath, can be visited by appointment, including out of hours.

considerations: Whether a pod needs planning permission depends on its size, its use and your site. The Pod Factory advises asking your local planning department; it also publishes its own guidance on the newer exemptions. A pod you live in is treated differently from a garden studio.
Pods arrive finished and are lifted in by crane, so there has to be a route for the lorry and the crane.
The base and groundworks are done before delivery. Agree who does them and what they cost before you sign.

The pods are framed in light gauge steel made by the supplier's sister company, Metal Frame Construction, which the supplier says holds NSAI and UKAS accreditations. Ask for the certificates that apply to your build.
